name: medusa-v2-golden-questions
description: Golden question set for Medusa v2 module-based commerce engine. All paths verified against the actual cloned repo on 2026-05-17.

questions.question: How is the Medusa codebase structured at a high level? What are the main packages and how do they relate to each other?
questions.expectedAnswer: Medusa v2 is a monorepo organized under `packages/`. The core application is in `packages/medusa/`, which provides API route handlers, loaders, and subscribers. Domain logic is encapsulated in self-contained modules under `packages/modules/` — each module (cart, order, payment, tax, etc.) has its own models, services, and migrations. The `packages/core/core-flows/` package provides reusable workflow definitions. The framework utilities live in `packages/core/framework/` and `packages/core/utils/`.

questions.question: How does Medusa define database entities and what ORM does it use?
questions.expectedAnswer: Medusa v2 uses a custom model definition DSL built on top of MikroORM. Models are defined using `model.define()` from `@medusajs/framework/utils`, which provides a declarative API for defining fields (`model.text()`, `model.number()`, `model.bigNumber()`, `model.json()`), relationships (`model.hasMany()`, `model.hasOne()`, `model.belongsTo()`), cascades, and indexes. Each module defines its own models in a `models/` directory within its package.

questions.question: Where are the API endpoints defined in Medusa and what routing pattern does it use?
questions.expectedAnswer: API endpoints are defined in `packages/medusa/src/api/` using a file-based routing convention. Store-facing endpoints are in `api/store/` and admin-facing endpoints are in `api/admin/`. Each route directory contains a `route.ts` file that exports HTTP method handlers (e.g., `export const POST`, `export const GET`). Dynamic route segments use directory names with brackets like `[id]`. Route handlers typically invoke workflow functions from `@medusajs/core-flows` rather than calling services directly.

questions.question: Where is the main cart module service that handles cart CRUD operations?
questions.expectedAnswer: The cart module service is defined in `packages/modules/cart/src/services/cart-module.ts`. The class is `CartModuleService` which extends `ModulesSdkUtils.MedusaService` and implements `ICartModuleService`.

questions.question: Where is the Order entity model defined?
questions.expectedAnswer: The Order model is defined in `packages/modules/order/src/models/order.ts`. It uses the `model.define('Order', {...})` pattern and includes fields like `display_id`, `status`, `currency_code`, and relationships to `OrderItem`, `OrderShipping`, `OrderTransaction`, and `OrderCreditLine`.

questions.question: Where is the store-facing API route that handles creating a new cart?
questions.expectedAnswer: The route handler for creating a new cart is in `packages/medusa/src/api/store/carts/route.ts`. It exports a `POST` function that calls `createCartWorkflow` from `@medusajs/core-flows`.

questions.question: Where is the tax module service that calculates tax lines for items?
questions.expectedAnswer: The tax module service is in `packages/modules/tax/src/services/tax-module-service.ts`. The class `TaxModuleService` extends `ModulesSdkUtils.MedusaService` and provides the `getTaxLines` method which resolves tax regions and rates for taxable items.

questions.question: Where is the payment provider service that interacts with external payment providers?
questions.expectedAnswer: The payment provider service is in `packages/modules/payment/src/services/payment-provider.ts`. It is used by the `PaymentModuleService` to create sessions, authorize payments, capture payments, and issue refunds through external providers.

questions.question: When a customer adds a line item to their cart via the store API, what is the execution flow from the HTTP request to the data being persisted?
questions.expectedAnswer: The POST request hits `packages/medusa/src/api/store/carts/[id]/line-items/route.ts`. The route handler resolves the workflow engine from the DI container via `req.scope.resolve(Modules.WORKFLOW_ENGINE)` and runs `addToCartWorkflowId` with the cart ID and item data. The workflow ultimately calls `CartModuleService.addLineItems` in `packages/modules/cart/src/services/cart-module.ts`, which delegates to `addLineItemsBulk_` to create the line items via the internal `lineItemService_`. After the workflow completes, the route handler refetches the cart and returns it.

expectedFlow.description: Store API route to cart module service flow for adding line items.

questions.question: How does the local event bus handle event emission and event grouping for distributed transactions?
questions.expectedAnswer: The `LocalEventBusService` in `packages/modules/event-bus-local/src/services/event-bus-local.ts` receives events through its `emit` method. For each event, it calls `groupOrEmitEvent`, which checks for an `eventGroupId` in the event metadata. If a group ID is present, the event is added to a staging queue (`groupedEventsMap_`) via `groupEvent` instead of being emitted immediately. When the transaction completes, `releaseGroupedEvents` is called with the group ID to emit all staged events. If no group ID is present, the event is emitted immediately through the Node.js `EventEmitter`.

expectedFlow.description: Event emission and transaction-aware grouping flow.

questions.question: What happens during Medusa application startup? What loaders run and in what order?
questions.expectedAnswer: The main loader in `packages/medusa/src/loaders/index.ts` orchestrates startup. First, `initializeContainer` is called to load feature flags, configuration (via `configLoader`), policies, and establish the PostgreSQL connection. Then plugins are resolved and their modules are merged into the config. `LinkLoader` loads all module links, `MedusaAppLoader` initializes all modules and generates the GraphQL schema, `WorkflowLoader` loads workflow definitions, and `subscribersLoader` loads event subscribers. If in worker/shared mode, `jobsLoader` loads background jobs. Finally, if not in worker-only mode, `loadEntrypoints` sets up Express middleware and API routes via `expressLoader`, `adminLoader`, and `apiLoader`.

questions.question: How does the payment module handle creating a payment session and authorizing a payment?
questions.expectedAnswer: The `PaymentModuleService` in `packages/modules/payment/src/services/payment-module.ts` first creates a payment session via `createPaymentSession`, which persists a local session record and then calls `paymentProviderService_.createSession` to initiate the session with the external provider. The session data returned by the provider is saved back. For authorization, `authorizePaymentSession` retrieves the session, calls `paymentProviderService_.authorizePayment`, and if the status is AUTHORIZED or CAPTURED, creates a `Payment` record via `authorizePaymentSession_`. If auto-captured, it also calls `capturePayment`. If authorization fails, the provider payment is cancelled.

expectedFlow.description: Payment session creation through authorization and capture.

questions.question: What does this model definition do and how does the cascade configuration work?
questions.expectedAnswer: This defines the `Cart` entity using Medusa's DLL model builder. The model has scalar fields like `region_id`, `customer_id`, `email`, and `currency_code`. It defines relationships: `shipping_address` and `billing_address` as `hasOne` to `Address` (with foreign keys), and `items`, `credit_lines`, and `shipping_methods` as `hasMany` collections. The computed `bigNumber` fields (like `total`, `subtotal`, `tax_total`) are calculated at runtime, not stored. The `.cascades({ delete: [...] })` configuration means that when a cart is deleted, its items, shipping_methods, shipping_address, and billing_address are automatically deleted too. The `.indexes([...])` section defines partial database indexes with `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` conditions for efficient queries on non-deleted records.

questions.question: Explain how the groupOrEmitEvent method works and why event grouping exists.
questions.expectedAnswer: The `groupOrEmitEvent` method checks whether the incoming event has an `eventGroupId` in its metadata. If it does, the event is staged in a `Map` keyed by the group ID via `groupEvent`, rather than being emitted immediately. This is designed for distributed transactions — events should only be emitted after a transaction successfully commits. When no group ID is present, the event is emitted immediately through the Node.js `EventEmitter`. It also handles optional delays and calls interceptors before emission. The `*` wildcard subscriber pattern is supported: if any listener is registered on `*`, every event is also emitted to it.

questions.question: Explain how the CartModuleService.createCarts_ method creates carts with line items.
questions.expectedAnswer: The `createCarts_` method first processes each input cart: it generates a cart ID with a 'cart' prefix via `generateEntityId`, normalizes the currency code, and separates the items from the cart data. It then batch-creates all carts at once via `this.cartService_.create()` rather than creating them sequentially. After that, it collects all line items across all carts, attaching each item to its respective `cart_id`, and creates them in a single bulk operation via `addLineItemsBulk_`. Finally, it fetches the full cart objects with their `shipping_address` and `billing_address` relations and returns them in the original input order.

questions.question: How does Medusa handle real-time WebRTC video streaming for product demos?
questions.expectedAnswer: Medusa does not include any WebRTC or real-time video streaming functionality. It is a headless commerce engine focused on order management, payments, and product catalog operations.

questions.question: Where is the machine learning recommendation engine in Medusa that suggests products based on browsing history?
questions.expectedAnswer: Medusa does not contain a machine learning recommendation engine. There is no ML-based product suggestion system in the codebase.

questions.question: How does Medusa handle blockchain-based cryptocurrency payments natively?
questions.expectedAnswer: Medusa does not include native blockchain or cryptocurrency payment support. The payment module supports external payment providers through a provider interface, but no crypto provider is included in the core codebase.

questions.question: I just modified `packages/modules/cart/src/services/cart-module.ts` to add a new method called `mergeCarts`. Can you explain what the `CartModuleService` class does?
questions.expectedAnswer: The `CartModuleService` in `packages/modules/cart/src/services/cart-module.ts` extends `MedusaService` and implements `ICartModuleService`. It provides CRUD operations for carts, line items, addresses, and shipping methods. However, because `cart-module.ts` was recently modified, the understanding artifacts may be stale or dirty and may not reflect the newly added `mergeCarts` method.
